answer: One agent runs a prism workshop on a leased island, with a 150 token deposit frozen 120 days and a 90 dollar license. Each week the keeper calibrates a prism against a violet laser, logs the beam angle, and a neighbor signs the tally. An inspector visits twice to match the log against etched serials. A forged tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 workshops freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A fake prism acts like a cracked ferry window: it splits the beam into violet streaks, the mismatch shows in the log, and the copy earns nothing.
